messages:
eva: Heads-up from today's KMS audit: a restore test failed because several historical DB snapshot objects under gs://redwood-tenant-backups/legacy/2019/ do not have our x-encrypt-meta and also appear to have been re-wrapped with an old KMS key that was retired during the 2022 rotation.

mike: Ouch. So two problems: missing internal metadata our restore tooling expects, and a kmsKeyName that points to an archived/disabled key. Paths?

eva: Sample objects:
- legacy/2019/db-tenant42-2019-08-21.sql.gz
- legacy/2019/db-tenant42-2019-11-12-part2.dump

`gsutil ls -L gs://redwood-tenant-backups/legacy/2019/db-tenant42-2019-08-21.sql.gz` shows `kmsKeyName: projects/project/locations/global/keyRings/kr/cryptoKeys/old_ck` and no x-encrypt-meta header. Attempting restore returned KMS permission error when our restore runner tried to decrypt.

rachel: Who owns old_ck? That key was rotated out and we revoked external grants last quarter. We probably didn't update the metadata flow for legacy re-wraps.

encops-bot: ALERT: kms_key_retired + missing_meta detected (count=2) in redwood-tenant-backups/legacy/2019. Recommended: audit key rotation events, create ephemeral decrypt grants for restore ops, and plan rewrap to current CMEK.

sre-oncall: Immediate triage: 1) check Cloud KMS audit logs for old_ck retire date and which principal performed the rewrap, 2) search Cloud Storage insert/update logs for rewrite events that changed kmsKeyName, 3) if restore urgent for a customer, create an ephemeral grant scoped to the restore job and log grant id.

eva: KMS audit shows old_ck scheduleDestroy at 2022-10-10, and a rewrite job in 2021-09 by `migration-tool@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com` that copied objects and set kmsKeyName to old_ck. The original uploader had left in 2019. So these were rewrapped mid-2021 to old_ck.

mike: That explains the failure. For immediate restore we can create a KMS cryptoKeyVersions.getPublic or a decrypt grant? In GCP you create an IAM binding for `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` for the service account doing the restore. But since key is scheduled for destroy we may need to use a key ring backup or key recovery flow with compliance/legal.

rachel: We should not re-enable old_ck widely. Short-term: create an ephemeral grant on old_ck limited to the restore SA with TTL, use it to decrypt to a staging area, then rewrap to current_ck and set x-encrypt-meta properly. Record the grant ID and approval in the ENCRYPT-OPS ticket.

encops-bot: REMINDER: ephemeral KMS grants must be logged. Use TTL 1h and submit approval record to ENCRYPT-OPS. Also include KMS operation ids in escrow manifest.

sre-oncall: Also run a global scan for any objects that reference old_ck to find scope. Use this Cloud Logging query:
```
resource.type=\"gcs_bucket\"
protoPayload.methodName=\"storage.objects.rewrite\"
protoPayload.request.metadata.kmsKeyName: \"old_ck\"
timestamp>=\"2021-01-01T00:00:00Z\" AND timestamp<\"2022-12-31T23:59:59Z\"
```

eva: Running the scan now. Found 14 objects across tenant buckets referencing old_ck; 9 are snapshots tied to active tenants.

mike: Priority: any active-tenant snapshots first. Create ephemeral grants for those restores only. For bulk remediation, plan a controlled rewrap: read object -> rewrite to current_ck -> set x-encrypt-meta with JSON like `{\"wrapped_by\":\"migration-tool-2021\",\"original_key\":\"old_ck\"}` so we keep provenance.

rachel: Important: the rewrap operation will emit new storage.objects.insert/rewrite events and KMS decrypt/encrypt calls, so ensure we capture those audit ids in the escrow manifest. Also schedule rate limiting to avoid KMS quota spikes.

encops-bot: SUGGESTION: use a worker pool with backoff and per-key rate cap. Store escrow manifest entries as lines: `object_path | original_insert_event | old_kmsKeyName | rewrap_event_id | kms_grant_ids` and save to gs://encrypt-ops-escrow/retrospective_manifests/ with CMEK protection.

sre-oncall: Legal/compliance - tagging you to approve ephemeral grant for tenant restore if needed. We should only grant decrypt for the minimum necessary time and log approval.

compliance: Acknowledge. We will require a one-line justification in the ticket and that the grant TTL is <= 2 hours. Also require that rewraps preserve provenance metadata in x-encrypt-meta.

eva: Action items summary: 
- eva: finish scan and produce list of objects referencing old_ck (EOD).
- mike: prepare ephemeral grant playbook and automated revoke script; test on one object (today).
- rachel: plan bulk rewrap job with rate limits and ensure new metadata includes provenance (week).
- sre-oncall: update restore runbook to handle kmsKeyName retired errors and fallback to escalate flow.

mike: Test ephemeral grant succeeded for one tenant snapshot, logged grant id G-20240301-01, restore to staging worked, rewrap to current_ck completed and x-encrypt-meta added.

eva: Great. I'll open ENCRYPT-OPS-901 and attach the object list + KMS audit pointers + the grant approval. Set priority P1 for tenant-impacting items and P3 for historical-only objects.

encops-bot: REMINDER: if any object had public reads historically, escalate to #incidents. Scan historical access logs for GETs to listed objects.

rachel: Ran quick search -> no public GETs. Reads were internal and vendor-service accounts only. We'll proceed with remediation and keep Compliance/Legal posted.

sre-oncall: Thanks team. Keep an eye on KMS request quotas during rewrap and post status to #eng-security when bulk job starts. If anything unexpected occurs escalate. :lock:
